svg.text: IP Address Filter — Low Level Design
Allow / Deny requests by client IP using CIDR rules, longest-prefix match (binary trie), LRU decision cache and lock-free reads
Rule Update Flow (admin changes rules without blocking readers)
Middleware extracts client IP (X-Forwarded-For only from trusted proxy, else remote addr).
Convert IPv4 / IPv6 text to a 32 / 128-bit value. Invalid format → reject (400).
Hit → return cached ALLOW / DENY immediately and skip matching (hot IPs are O(1)).
matcher.match(ip) walks the binary trie bit by bit and collects matching CIDR rules.
Longest prefix (most specific) wins; tie → higher priority; tie → DENY beats ALLOW.
Apply default policy: allowlist mode → DENY, blocklist mode → ALLOW.
Store decision in cache; log (ip, ruleId, decision, timestamp) for audit / metrics.
ALLOW → pass to next handler / backend. DENY → 403 Forbidden.
Readers never block: they use the current immutable trie snapshot; writers build a new trie and swap the reference atomically.
Example: 10.0.0.0/8 DENY + 10.1.0.0/16 ALLOW → 10.1.5.9 is ALLOWED (/16 is more specific), 10.9.9.9 is DENIED.
Multi-node setup: nodes poll repo.version() or listen to pub/sub, then rebuild their local trie.
Strategy pattern: IPMatcher is pluggable (trie, range list, GeoIP).
Binary trie gives longest-prefix match in O(32) / O(128), independent of rule count.
Copy-on-write snapshot: lock-free reads, safe concurrent updates.
LRU cache with TTL absorbs repeated IPs; cleared on every rule change.
Trust X-Forwarded-For only from known proxies (prevents IP spoofing).
Fail-safe: define default policy and fail-open / fail-closed behaviour.
